newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai 1996 exports seen below target - ministry.
newsitem.headline: Thai 1996 exports seen below target - ministry.

text.p: Thailand's exports this year are projected to total 1.45 trillion baht ($58 billion), well below the targeted 1.60 trillion baht, a senior commerce ministry official said on Tuesday.

Thawatchai Sophastienphong, deputy chief of the ministry's department of business economics, told reporters that exports grew only 3.1 percent during the first eight months of 1996 over the year-ago period.
"Export growth was limited by a slowdown in industrial goods exports. Some other traditional foreign revenue earners also slowed," he said.
The central bank said last month that in the first eight months exports grew at a rate of 2.4 percent against the same period in 1995.
The Bank of Thailand's figures are regarded as the official data for the nation.
In all of 1995, Thailand's exports grew 23.6 percent to 1.38 trillion baht, according to the bank.
But Thawatchai predicted recovery in the near future thanks to government measures to strenghten exports, including tax rebates and lower tariffs on raw materials.
Commerce ministry sources said representatives of the private and public sectors would meet in December on the export outlook and to set a target for 1997.
